Assume the beam is straight, prismatic, homogeneous, isotropic, and linear-elastic with Young's modulus E.
Assume small deformations and Euler-Bernoulli beam theory, so plane sections remain plane and perpendicular to the neutral axis.
Use a rectangular cross-section with width b in the local z-direction and height h in the local y-direction, with the centroid and neutral axis located at y = 0.
Use the sign convention that positive internal bending moment M_z produces compressive normal stress at positive y and tensile normal stress at negative y.
At any section where the internal bending moment is M_z, the bending stress at an arbitrary fiber located a distance y from the neutral axis is sigma_x(y) = -M_z y / I_z, where I_z = b h^3 / 12.
The neutral axis is the location where sigma_x = 0.
The bending stress varies linearly through the cross-section thickness.
The maximum bending stress magnitude occurs at the extreme fibers y = +h/2 and y = -h/2, and is sigma_max = |M_z| h / (2 I_z) = 6 |M_z| / (b h^2).
The corresponding bending strain at a fiber y is epsilon_x(y) = sigma_x(y) / E = -M_z y / (E I_z).
The curvature of the centroidal axis due to the bending moment is kappa = M_z / (E I_z), and the radius of curvature is rho = E I_z / M_z.
If a transverse shear force V exists from the bending load, the shear stress at an arbitrary depth y in a rectangular section is tau_xy(y) = V Q(y) / (I_z b), where Q(y) = (b/2)(h^2/4 - y^2).
Ignore axial force, torsion, stress concentrations, local end effects, and large-deformation effects unless explicitly specified.
